items.reason: This paper focuses on accelerating attention mechanisms on GPUs, specifically Hopper, by exploiting asynchrony, warp-specialization, and block quantization, directly aligning with interests in GPU kernels, AI hardware, and quantization for LLMs.

This work proposes GPTQ, a post-training quantization method to reduce the computational and storage costs of large GPT models, directly addressing interests in quantization and LLM inference on AI hardware.

This paper introduces T2Quant, a task and time-aware quantization framework for Diffusion Language Models, focusing on optimizing precision across denoising steps to reduce computational costs, relevant to quantization and LLM inference.
This paper explores the synergy between reasoning and acting in LLMs, proposing an interleaved approach for greater synergy, which is relevant to agent capabilities and LLM development.
This paper introduces SWE-bench, an evaluation framework for LLMs on real-world software engineering tasks, which is relevant to evaluating agent capabilities and LLM development.

This paper presents EvalResearchBench, a benchmark for autonomous evaluation research, aiming to enable AI agents to automate benchmark design for recursive self-improvement, relevant to agent research.
This paper studies model ability and task-conditioned collaboration with humans in language-model agents, exploring the division of labor and human involvement, relevant to agent capabilities.
This paper introduces TARSphere, a framework for embodied agents in evolving environments, focusing on physical and social constraints, which is adjacent to agent research.
This paper presents WeVisOne-VL, a unified visual perception model for various visual tasks, which is an adjacent discovery in AI research but not directly related to the core interests.
This paper introduces SplatLab, an autonomous research system for 3D Gaussian Splatting, which is an adjacent discovery in AI research and agent systems.
